quote: A standard horror film from start to finish, Corin Hardy’s "Whistle" benefits from a game cast and a third act that contains some clever narrative switchbacks.

The death whistle comes with endless creative possibilities for scares, and Corin Hardy & Owen Egerton make the most of it. Whistle is the complete young adult horror package — great cast, clever concept, excellent execution, and a winning nostalgic feel.
Whistle is an effective, nasty slasher that delivers a new riff on the Final Destination blueprint, finding inventive and entertaining ways to send its characters to the afterlife.
Whistle brings brutality back to teenage horror, delivering a nostalgic feel with modern sensibilities.
Featuring incredible kill sequences and strong performances, Corin Hardy’s ‘Whistle’ is a deeply effective piece of teen-centric horror storytelling.
Whistle is, at its best, a lively and ferocious teenage slasher ditty that brings that breakneck overdrive appeal ... an engaging rearrangement of Final Destination.
By the end, Whistle feels less like a horror story and more like a frustrating exercise in wasted potential.

Horror can turn camp very easily and we can also have horror films that don’t take their audience seriously. Whistle does none of this but instead feels like a nod to the classics while being original and fun.
As both a generic knock-off and a borderline-offensive use of Latino culture, Corin Hardy’s latest film is pretty unforgivable — even by the typically very low standards of the teen horror genre.
WHISTLE is simple, effective, scary, and fun. What else could you ask for?
